documents.title: MAUD deal points pack — Merger Agreement (Meridian Compass / Halcyon Therapeutics) execution version — Article II consideration and Article VIII termination excerpt
documents.body:
AGREEMENT AND PLAN OF MERGER, dated as of June 2, 2026 (this "Agreement"), by and among Meridian Compass Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Parent"), MC Falcon Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent ("Merger Sub"), and Halcyon Therapeutics, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Company"). Conformed excerpt of Article II (Merger Consideration) and Article VIII (Termination; Remedies) from the EXECUTION VERSION, prepared by Ellsworth & Crane LLP for the deal-points file. This excerpt supersedes all prior drafts, including draft No. 3 circulated May 11, 2026.

Section 2.1 Merger Consideration. Each share of Company Common Stock issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time (other than Excluded Shares and Dissenting Shares) shall be converted into the right to receive $28.50 in cash, without interest (the "Merger Consideration"). The Merger is a one-step merger under Section 251 of the DGCL; adoption of this Agreement by the affirmative vote of the holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of Company Common Stock (the "Company Stockholder Approval") is the only vote of Company stockholders required.

Section 8.1 Termination. This Agreement may be terminated at any time prior to the Effective Time: (a) by mutual written consent of Parent and the Company; (b) by either Parent or the Company if the Merger shall not have been consummated on or before March 31, 2027 (the "Outside Date"); provided, that if on such date each condition other than the Regulatory Condition has been satisfied or waived, the Outside Date shall automatically be extended to June 30, 2027; (c) by the Company, prior to receipt of the Company Stockholder Approval, in order to enter into a definitive agreement providing for a Superior Proposal, subject to compliance with Section 5.4 and concurrent payment of the Company Termination Fee; or (d) by Parent, if the Company Board shall have effected an Adverse Recommendation Change.

Section 8.2 Company Termination Fee. In the event this Agreement is terminated pursuant to Section 8.1(c) or Section 8.1(d), the Company shall pay to Parent a fee of $125,000,000 in cash (the "Company Termination Fee"). The Company Termination Fee shall also become payable if (i) an Acquisition Proposal has been publicly disclosed after the date hereof and not withdrawn, (ii) this Agreement is thereafter terminated pursuant to Section 8.1(b) or on account of the Company's uncured material breach, and (iii) within twelve (12) months after such termination (the "Tail Period") the Company consummates, or enters into a definitive agreement providing for, any Acquisition Proposal (with fifty percent (50%) substituted for the twenty percent (20%) thresholds in the definition thereof). In no event shall the Company Termination Fee be payable more than once.

Section 8.3 Parent Termination Fee. In the event this Agreement is terminated (i) by either party pursuant to Section 8.1(b) at a time when the Regulatory Condition has not been satisfied but each other condition has been satisfied or waived, or (ii) by the Company because Parent has failed to consummate the Closing when required by Section 1.2, Parent shall pay to the Company a fee of $265,000,000 in cash (the "Parent Termination Fee"). In no event shall the Company be entitled to receive both the Parent Termination Fee and a grant of specific performance compelling consummation of the Merger.

Section 8.4 Specific Performance. The parties agree that irreparable damage would occur if any provision of this Agreement were not performed in accordance with its specific terms, and that each party shall be entitled to an injunction or injunctions to prevent breaches of this Agreement and to enforce specifically the terms and provisions hereof — including, for the avoidance of doubt, the right of the Company to cause Parent and Merger Sub to consummate the Merger — in each case without proof of damages, this being in addition to any other remedy at law or in equity.

documents.title: MAUD deal points pack — Halcyon Therapeutics merger agreement conformed provisions — MAE definition, interim operating covenant and non-solicitation (Sections 1.1, 5.1, 5.4)
documents.body:
CONFORMED PROVISIONS MEMORANDUM — Halcyon Therapeutics / Meridian Compass Agreement and Plan of Merger dated June 2, 2026. Sections 1.1 (selected definition), 5.1 (interim operating covenant) and 5.4 (non-solicitation). Prepared by Ellsworth & Crane LLP knowledge management for the annual public-target deal-points survey. Quoted language is verbatim from the execution version.

1. Definition of "Company Material Adverse Effect" (Section 1.1). "Company Material Adverse Effect" means any change, event, occurrence or effect that has had, or would reasonably be expected to have, a material adverse effect on the business, financial condition or results of operations of the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole; provided, however, that no change, event, occurrence or effect arising out of or resulting from any of the following shall constitute, or be taken into account in determining whether there has been, a Company Material Adverse Effect: (i) general economic, credit, capital or financial market conditions; (ii) conditions generally affecting the industries in which the Company and its Subsidiaries operate; (iii) any change in Law, GAAP or the interpretation or enforcement thereof; (iv) any epidemic, pandemic or other public health event (including COVID-19 and any COVID-19 Measures or other governmental responses thereto); (v) any acts of war, armed hostilities, sabotage, terrorism, natural disasters or other force majeure events; (vi) the negotiation, execution, announcement or pendency of this Agreement; (vii) any failure by the Company to meet any internal or published projections, forecasts or revenue or earnings predictions (it being understood that the underlying causes of any such failure may be taken into account unless otherwise excluded by this definition); or (viii) any action taken at the written request of Parent or expressly required by this Agreement; provided, further, that any change, event, occurrence or effect referred to in clauses (i), (ii), (iv) or (v) above shall be taken into account in determining whether a Company Material Adverse Effect has occurred to the extent it has a disproportionate impact on the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, relative to other participants in the industries in which the Company and its Subsidiaries operate. Survey-grid note: the pandemic carveout in clause (iv) IS subject to the disproportionate-impact modifier; the change-in-Law carveout in clause (iii) is not.

2. Interim Operating Covenant (Section 5.1). From the date of this Agreement until the Effective Time, except as consented to in writing by Parent, the Company shall, and shall cause each of its Subsidiaries to, conduct its business in all material respects in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to preserve substantially intact its business organization and its material business relationships.

3. Non-Solicitation; Fiduciary Exception; Matching Rights (Section 5.4). From and after the date of this Agreement, the Company shall not, and shall cause its Subsidiaries and Representatives not to, directly or indirectly solicit, initiate or knowingly encourage or facilitate any Acquisition Proposal. Notwithstanding the foregoing, at any time prior to receipt of the Company Stockholder Approval, if the Company receives a bona fide written Acquisition Proposal that did not result from a breach of this Section 5.4, and the Company Board determines in good faith, after consultation with outside legal counsel and its financial advisor, that such Acquisition Proposal constitutes or would reasonably be expected to lead to a Superior Proposal and that the failure to take such action would be inconsistent with the directors' fiduciary duties under applicable Law, the Company may furnish information pursuant to an Acceptable Confidentiality Agreement and participate in negotiations with the Person making such proposal. Prior to effecting any Adverse Recommendation Change or terminating to accept a Superior Proposal, the Company shall give Parent four (4) Business Days' prior written notice and shall negotiate in good faith with Parent during such period (the "Match Period"); a new notice with an additional three (3) Business Days' Match Period is required for each material amendment to the financial terms of such Superior Proposal.

documents.title: MAUD deal points pack — Merger Agreement (Aurelian Summit / Silverline Data Systems) execution version — tender offer terms, Offer conditions and MAE definition excerpt
documents.body:
CONFORMED EXCERPT — AGREEMENT AND PLAN OF MERGER, dated as of July 20, 2026, by and among Aurelian Summit Group plc, a public limited company organized under the laws of England and Wales ("Parent"), Summit Argent Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Parent ("Purchaser"), and Silverline Data Systems, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Company"). Excerpt of Article I (the Offer), Article VI (Conditions to the Offer) and the definition of Company Material Adverse Effect, prepared for the deal-points file by Ellsworth & Crane LLP from the EXECUTION VERSION.

Section 1.1 The Offer. Provided that this Agreement shall not have been terminated in accordance with Article VIII, Purchaser shall commence (within the meaning of Rule 14d-2 under the Exchange Act), as promptly as practicable and in any event within ten (10) Business Days after the date hereof, a tender offer (the "Offer") to purchase all of the issued and outstanding shares of Company Common Stock at a price per share of $47.25, net to the seller in cash, without interest (the "Offer Price"). This is a two-step transaction: as soon as practicable following the Acceptance Time, the Merger shall be effected without a vote of the Company's stockholders pursuant to Section 251(h) of the DGCL, and each share not accepted in the Offer (other than Excluded Shares and Dissenting Shares) shall be converted into the right to receive the Offer Price.

Section 6.1 Conditions to the Offer. Notwithstanding any other provision of the Offer, Purchaser shall not be required to accept for payment any shares of Company Common Stock validly tendered unless, at the scheduled Expiration Time: (a) the number of shares validly tendered and not validly withdrawn, together with shares owned by Parent and its Subsidiaries, represents at least a majority of the shares of Company Common Stock then outstanding (the "Minimum Condition"); (b) the waiting period under the HSR Act shall have expired or been terminated and the requisite foreign direct investment clearances obtained (the "Regulatory Condition"); (c) since the date of this Agreement there shall not have occurred a Company Material Adverse Effect that is continuing; and (d) the aggregate number of shares of Company Common Stock with respect to which the holders thereof have properly exercised and not withdrawn or lost appraisal rights under Section 262 of the DGCL (the "Dissenting Shares") shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the shares of Company Common Stock outstanding immediately prior to the Expiration Time (the "Appraisal Rights Condition").

Section 8.1(b) Outside Date. Either Parent or the Company may terminate this Agreement if the Acceptance Time shall not have occurred on or before November 14, 2026 (the "Outside Date"), automatically extended to February 14, 2027 if on such date the Regulatory Condition (but no other condition) remains unsatisfied.

Definition — "Company Material Adverse Effect" (condensed). The definition follows the customary two-part structure, with carveouts for: general economic and financial market conditions; conditions generally affecting the Company's industry; changes in Law or GAAP; epidemics, pandemics and other public health events; acts of war, terrorism and natural disasters; the announcement or pendency of the transactions; and failure to meet projections. The disproportionate-impact modifier applies only to the economic-conditions, industry-conditions and war/terrorism carveouts; it does NOT apply to the change-in-Law or pandemic carveouts in this agreement.

documents.title: MAUD deal points pack — Silverline Data Systems deal protection and termination note to file (Sections 5.1, 5.3, 7.3 and 8.9)
documents.body:
NOTE TO FILE — Silverline Data Systems / Aurelian Summit Group: deal protection, interim covenant and termination provisions, conformed from the execution version of the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated July 20, 2026 (Sections 5.1, 5.3, 7.3 and 8.9). Prepared by Ellsworth & Crane LLP for the deal-points survey grid. For the avoidance of doubt in the survey grid: this agreement contains NO go-shop provision of any kind; the non-solicitation covenant applies from execution of the Agreement, and there is no post-signing window during which the Company may solicit competing proposals.

Section 5.1 Interim Operating Covenant. From the date of the Agreement until the earlier of the Effective Time and termination, except with Parent's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to conduct its business in the ordinary course of business and to preserve intact its material business relationships. Drafting note: unlike the market-majority formulation, this covenant does NOT include a "consistent with past practice" qualifier.

Section 5.3 No Solicitation; Fiduciary Exception; Matching Rights. From and after the date of the Agreement, the Company shall not, and shall cause its Representatives not to, solicit, initiate or knowingly facilitate any Acquisition Proposal. Prior to the Acceptance Time, in response to a bona fide unsolicited written Acquisition Proposal that the Company Board determines in good faith (after consultation with outside counsel and its financial advisor) constitutes or would reasonably be expected to lead to a Superior Proposal, and where failure to act would be inconsistent with the directors' fiduciary duties under applicable Law, the Company may furnish information under an Acceptable Confidentiality Agreement and engage in discussions. Before any Adverse Recommendation Change or fiduciary termination, the Company must give Parent five (5) Business Days' prior written notice and negotiate in good faith during that period (the "Match Period"); each subsequent material modification to the financial terms of the Superior Proposal triggers a new notice and an additional two (2) Business Days' Match Period.

Section 7.3 Company Termination Fee. Upon (a) a fiduciary termination by the Company to accept a Superior Proposal, (b) termination by Parent following an Adverse Recommendation Change, or (c) a tail-period transaction (an Acquisition Proposal publicly made before termination and consummated, or made the subject of a definitive agreement, within nine (9) months after termination for Outside Date failure or Company breach), the Company shall pay Parent a termination fee of $86,500,000 in cash (the "Company Termination Fee"), payable at most once.

Section 8.9 Remedies. The parties' remedies are asymmetric. Parent and Purchaser are entitled to specific performance of the Company's covenants under Sections 5.1 and 5.3. The Company, however, is NOT entitled to specific performance to compel Parent or Purchaser to commence or consummate the Offer or to effect the Closing; the Company's sole and exclusive remedy against Parent and Purchaser for any failure to consummate the Offer or the Merger is an action for monetary damages, capped at $150,000,000 in the aggregate (the "Parent Liability Cap"). No separate reverse termination fee is provided.

documents.title: MAUD deal points pack — Halcyon Therapeutics merger agreement draft No. 3 (SUPERSEDED) — prior termination-fee construct
documents.body:
DRAFT No. 3 — May 11, 2026 — SUPERSEDED; retained for the negotiation history file only. Do not cite for current deal points; the execution version dated June 2, 2026 controls.

Excerpt of draft Article VIII, Halcyon Therapeutics / Meridian Compass Agreement and Plan of Merger, reflecting Parent's counsel's markup before the June 1 all-hands call.

Draft Section 8.1(b): the Merger to be consummated on or before December 31, 2026 (the draft "Outside Date"), with a single three-month extension for the Regulatory Condition. [Rejected by the Company; the parties later agreed to a longer initial period.]

Draft Section 8.2: Company Termination Fee of $110,000,000, payable on fiduciary termination or following an Adverse Recommendation Change, with a fifteen (15) month tail. [The tail was shortened and the fee re-cut against the final equity value in the executed agreement.]

Draft Section 8.3: Parent Termination Fee of $240,000,000, payable only on antitrust failure. [The executed agreement broadened the trigger to include Parent's failure to close and increased the amount.]

Draft Section 5.4: matching rights of three (3) Business Days initial and two (2) Business Days for amendments. [Extended in the executed agreement.]

Negotiation note (A. Renfield, Ellsworth & Crane LLP): Company countered at 2.6% of equity value on the company-side fee; Parent's opening ask was 3.9%. The compromise reflected in the execution version was struck at the June 1 principals' call. All figures in this draft are of historical interest only and do not reflect the executed deal points.

documents.title: MAUD deal points pack — Lazuli Partners correspondence re Silverline termination-fee benchmarking
documents.body:
CORRESPONDENCE — from Lazuli Partners LLC (financial advisor to the Silverline Data Systems special committee) to the deal team distribution list; re: break-fee benchmarking ahead of the July 18, 2026 board meeting. Filed for the record; this letter is advisory only and does not state the terms of any executed agreement.

Team — ahead of Saturday's board session, our benchmarking of company-side termination fees in all-cash technology tender offers signed in the trailing twenty-four months shows a median of approximately 3.4% of fully diluted equity value. Applied to the equity value implied by the price under discussion, that median would imply a fee of roughly $92,000,000, with the interquartile range running from approximately $78,000,000 to $101,000,000. We would characterize anything at or below 3.5% as within the range the Delaware courts have routinely sustained.

On process structures: several recent sponsor-backed deals in the set paired a conventional no-shop with a 35-day go-shop window and a bifurcated fee (roughly half the full fee for a topping bid signed during or shortly after the go-shop). Given the breadth of the pre-signing outreach the committee ran — twenty-one logical buyers contacted under NDA — we do not believe a go-shop is necessary here and expect the buyer to resist one strenuously; whether the executed agreement includes any such construct is a matter for the definitive documentation, which counsel will summarize separately.

We will circulate the full comparables deck under separate cover. Please treat these figures as directional inputs to the committee's deliberation rather than as terms of the transaction.

— R. Okafor, Managing Director, Lazuli Partners LLC

documents.title: MAUD deal points pack — client alert: appraisal rights under Section 262 DGCL in two-step mergers (general guidance)
documents.body:
CLIENT ALERT — Ellsworth & Crane LLP, M&A practice group. Appraisal rights under Section 262 of the Delaware General Corporation Law in two-step tender-offer mergers: a refresher for deal teams. This alert is general guidance; it does not describe the terms of any particular pending transaction.

1. Availability. In a merger effected under Section 251(h), stockholders who do not tender and who perfect their rights under Section 262 may seek a judicial appraisal of the fair value of their shares. Because no stockholder vote occurs, the demand mechanics run from the notice of the merger rather than from a meeting record date, and strict compliance with the statutory timeline remains a trap for the unwary.

2. Appraisal closing conditions generally. Acquirors sometimes negotiate a condition that the offer need not be consummated if appraisal demands exceed a negotiated ceiling. In our recent experience, such ceilings most commonly fall at ten percent (10%) or twelve percent (12%) of outstanding shares, though both higher and lower formulations appear; many strategic buyers dispense with the condition entirely, and its presence, threshold and measurement date vary deal by deal. Whether any given agreement contains such a condition — and at what percentage — can be determined only from that agreement's conditions article.

3. Interaction with fee provisions. An appraisal condition is a closing condition, not a deal-protection device; its failure typically permits termination without any termination fee becoming payable, subject to the agreement's effect-of-termination section.

4. Practice pointers. (a) Diligence the holder base early: concentrated event-driven funds correlate with appraisal risk. (b) Model the interest-rate arbitrage under the post-2016 amendments, including the prepayment mechanic of Section 262(h). (c) In drafting, define Dissenting Shares by reference to demands properly exercised and not withdrawn or lost, and fix the measurement time at the offer's expiration. Questions may be directed to the M&A knowledge-management team.
